items.informal_name: Identity: $\text{ofFn}_n \circ \text{toFn}_n = \text{id}$ for Polynomials of Degree Less Than $n$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq R] {n : ℕ} {p : Polynomial R},
  p.natDegree < n → (Polynomial.ofFn n) ((Polynomial.toFn n) p) = p
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$ and polynomial $p$ over a semiring $R$ with natural degree less than $n$, the composition of the linear map converting finite sequences to polynomials and the coefficient extraction map results in the original polynomial $p$. In other words, $\text{ofFn}_n(\text{toFn}_n(p)) = p$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Polynomial Pairs with Bounded Degree Difference
items.type:
∀ {Fq : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Fq] [inst_1 : Ring Fq] {d m : ℕ},
  Fintype.card Fq ^ d ≤ m →
    ∀ (b : Polynomial Fq) (A : Fin m.succ → Polynomial Fq),
      (∀ (i : Fin m.succ), (A i).degree < b.degree) → ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ (A i₁ - A i₀).degree < ↑(b.natDegree - d)
items.informal_description: Given a finite ring $ Fq $ with cardinality $ q $, natural numbers $ d $ and $ m $ such that $ q^d \leq m $, a nonzero polynomial $ b \in Fq[X] $, and a function $ A: \mathrm{Fin}(m+1) \to Fq[X] $ where each $ A(i) $ has degree less than $ \deg(b) $, there exist distinct indices $ i_0, i_1 \in \mathrm{Fin}(m+1) $ such that the degree of $ A(i_1) - A(i_0) $ satisfies $ \deg(A(i_1) - A(i_0)) < \mathrm{natdeg}(b) - d $, where $ \mathrm{natdeg}(b) $ denotes the natural degree of $ b $ (equal to $ \deg(b) $ if nonzero, otherwise 0).

items.informal_name: Partitioning Polynomials with Bounded Differences Modulo a Non-Zero Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {Fq : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Fq] [inst_1 : Field Fq] (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ∀ {b : Polynomial Fq},
      b ≠ 0 →
        ∀ (A : Fin n → Polynomial Fq),
          ∃ t,
            ∀ (i₀ i₁ : Fin n),
              t i₀ = t i₁ → ↑(Polynomial.cardPowDegree (A i₁ % b - A i₀ % b)) < Polynomial.cardPowDegree b • ε
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, positive real number $\varepsilon$, non-zero polynomial $b \in \mathbb{F}_q[X]$, and sequence of $n$ polynomials $A_0, \ldots, A_{n-1} \in \mathbb{F}_q[X]$, there exists a partition function $t$ mapping indices $\{0, \ldots, n-1\}$ to $\left\lceil \frac{-\log \varepsilon}{\log |\mathbb{F}_q|} \right\rceil$ classes such that for any two indices $i_0, i_1$ in the same class, the difference $A_{i_1} \mod b - A_{i_0} \mod b$ has $\text{cardPowDegree}$ strictly less than $\varepsilon \cdot \text{cardPowDegree}(b)$. Here, $\text{cardPowDegree}$ denotes a degree-like measure combining field cardinality and polynomial degree, and $|\mathbb{F}_q|$ is the size of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] {S : Type u_4} [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S] {b : PowerSeries S},

items.informal_name: Substitution of a Monomial in Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] {τ : Type u_4} {S : Type u_5} [inst_1 : CommRing S]
  [inst_2 : Algebra R S] {a : σ → MvPowerSeries τ S},
  MvPowerSeries.HasSubst a →
    ∀ (e : σ →₀ ℕ) (r : R),
      MvPowerSeries.subst a ((MvPowerSeries.monomial e) r) =
        (algebraMap R (MvPowerSeries τ S)) r * e.prod fun s n => a s ^ n
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a commutative ring $ R $ in variables $ \sigma $, substituting each variable $ s \in \sigma $ with a power series $ a(s) $ in variables $ \tau $ over a ring $ S $, the substitution of the monomial $ r \cdot X^e $ (where $ e $ is a finite support function $ \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $) results in $ \phi(r) \cdot \prod_{s \in \text{support}(e)} (a(s))^{e(s)} $, where $ \phi: R \to S[[\tau]] $ is the canonical algebra homomorphism.

items.informal_name: Expansion of a Monomial in Multivariate Power Series Scales Exponents by p
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : Finite σ] [inst_1 : CommRing R] (p : ℕ) (hp : p ≠ 0) (d : σ →₀ ℕ) (r : R),
  (MvPowerSeries.expand p hp) ((MvPowerSeries.monomial d) r) = (MvPowerSeries.monomial (p • d)) r
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series over a commutative ring $ R $ in variables indexed by $ \sigma $, applying the expansion map $ \text{expand}_p $ to the monomial with exponent $ d : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $ and coefficient $ r \in R $ results in the monomial with exponent $ p \cdot d $ and the same coefficient $ r $. In symbols: $ \text{expand}_p(\text{monomial}_d(r)) = \text{monomial}_{p \cdot d}(r) $.

items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ),
  Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) (d : σ →₀ ℕ),
      MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.mapDomain f d) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ) = MvPolynomial.coeff d φ

This holds because injective renaming preserves monomial coefficients when variables are relabeled without collision.

items.informal_name: Evaluation Identity for Domain Mapping of Finite Support Functions under Injectivity
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] (S : Set α) {f : α → β} (x : α →₀ M),
  ↑x.support ⊆ S → Set.InjOn f S → ∀ {a : α}, a ∈ S → (Finsupp.mapDomain f x) (f a) = x a
items.informal_description: Let $ S $ be a subset of $ \alpha $, $ f : \alpha \to \beta $ a function, and $ x : \alpha \to_0 M $ a finite support function. If the support of $ x $ is contained in $ S $ and $ f $ is injective on $ S $, then for every $ a \in S $, the value of the domain-mapped function $ \mathrm{mapDomain}\, f\, x $ at $ f(a) $ equals $ x(a) $. In symbols: $ (\mathrm{mapDomain}\, f\, x)(f(a)) = x(a) $.

items.type:

  Set.InjOn f S → Set.InjOn (Finsupp.mapDomain f) {w | ↑w.support ⊆ S}
items.informal_description: If a function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $ is injective on a subset $ S \subseteq \alpha $, then the domain mapping operation $ \text{mapDomain} \, f $ is injective when restricted to the set of finite support functions $ \alpha \to_0 M $ whose supports are contained in $ S $.

items.type:

  Function.Injective f → ∀ (x : α →₀ M) (a : α), (Finsupp.mapDomain f x) (f a) = x a
items.informal_description: Given a function $ f : \alpha \to \beta $ and a finite support function $ x : \alpha \to_0 M $, this constructs a finite support function $ \beta \to_0 M $ by summing the values of $ x $ over all pre-images of each $ b \in \beta $ under $ f $. Specifically, for each $ b \in \beta $, the resulting function evaluates to $ \sum_{a \in f^{-1}(b)} x(a) $, with finite support inherited from $ x $.
